title.en: AP Calculus BC Exam Format & Units Overview

body.en: AP Calculus BC Exam Format & Units Overview covers essential College Board AP Calculus BC competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Exam Structure & AB Subscore Architecture

body.en: Master the two-section timing blueprint (Section I: 45 MCQs / 105 min, Section II: 6 FRQs / 90 min) and understand how the AB Subscore is calculated from shared curriculum items.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

The AP Calculus BC exam awards an AB Subscore in addition to the overall BC score. Which units and questions contribute to the AB Subscore?

solution.en: The AB Subscore is based exclusively on the questions on the BC exam that test shared material from Units 1 through 8 (Limits, Derivatives, Integrals, and Differential Equations). Approximately 60% of the BC exam questions contribute to the AB Subscore.

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Section Timing, Calculator Strategy & Scoring Weights

body.en: Navigate calculator transitions between sections and optimize point recovery on multi-part FRQs.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

On Section II, after the initial 30 minutes of Part A (Calculator), students must put away their graphing calculators for Part B (No Calculator). Are students permitted to continue working on Questions 1 and 2 during the remaining 60 minutes?

solution.en: Yes. Students may continue working on Questions 1 and 2 during Part B, but they may NOT use a calculator. They can write algebraic setups, justifications, or solve non-calculator parts.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Free-Response Synthesis & The 9-Point Rubric Standard

body.en: College Board FRQ rubrics award points strictly for setup, justification with theorems (MVT, EVT, FTC), units of measure, and exact 3-decimal rounding.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

On an AP Calculus BC FRQ, a student computes a definite integral numerically using a calculator and writes down \(14.821\) without showing the integral expression. How many points will the student earn for this response?

solution.en: The student will earn 0 points (or lose the answer point). College Board scoring guidelines explicitly mandate showing the mathematical setup (e.g. \(\int_0^4 f(t)\,dt\)) before stating any calculator-computed numerical value.
